Both inputs are CALLER-SUPPLIED; compile() only rejects all-zero digests (review F-08). The compiler does not hash its own bytes.
what_is_bound_in_circuit_today.effect_of_this_repair: A caller that supplies the successor BUILD-MANIFEST digest 4e3ba2e2... gets a different compiler_build_digest header constant than one supplying 2c943b51.... Header constants enter the binding constraints as Variable::One coefficients, so the R1CS matrices and ProbeReport::r1cs_sha256 of EVERY relation change with the supplied build digest even though no constraint-generating code changed. The exact new digests are computed by Core's canonical encoder at run time and are not computed or claimed here.

r04_disclosure.fact: compiler_source_manifest_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the whole BUILD-MANIFEST.json file. That file carries annotation bytes besides the 16 {path, sha256, bytes} entries: format, rule, origin_build_manifest_sha256 and a per-entry vs_origin_r2 label. compiler_build_digest = SHA-256(intent::canonical(CompilerBuild { compiler_source_manifest_sha256, core_closure_sha256 })), so a change to any annotation byte (for example re-pointing origin_build_manifest_sha256 or relabelling vs_origin_r2) changes compiler_build_digest, its header constant, the constant (Variable::One) coefficients of the header binding constraints of every relation and therefore every r1cs_sha256, with no compiled-code change.
r04_disclosure.format_unchanged: mori-r1cs-build-manifest/1 is kept exactly (same keys, same rule text, same annotation meaning: origin_build_manifest_sha256 = origin-r2 2c943b51..., vs_origin_r2 compared with the origin-r2 SOURCE-MANIFEST pins). Defining mori-r1cs-build-manifest/2 with {path, sha256, bytes} entries only is the other P-2 option; it is NOT done in this repair.
r04_disclosure.what_byte_identity_establishes: Which exact bytes were named. It establishes no source provenance, no build provenance (F-08: both CompilerBuild inputs remain caller-supplied), no semantic equivalence between builds and no security or funds-safety property. Equal digests are not acceptance; different digests are not a semantic change.
